title: What enumeration proposed and the kernel kept — 118 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
What enumeration proposed and the kernel kept. 118 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/imagined.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 1 definition is used by two or more theorems, binding 6903 pairs; the theorems fall into 1 strand. Most binding: m9 (118).

2 · Imports. Built on: z9.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 files: src/proof/imagined.lean, src/proof/z9.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 118 sealed receipts fold to 37fe0337-e772-8eb0-861c-2ee17049b0cf. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 4, 2, 5, 0, 7, 5). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: address.lean (41 observed, 25.31 expected, lift 1.62), energy.lean (46 observed, 28.34 expected, lift 1.62), merkaba.lean (13 observed, 8.1 expected, lift 1.61). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 1.71 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 57.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.52; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.51. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 78375f1a602d (2026-09-15), over 817 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. The doubling orbit 1,2,4,8,7,5 is the cyclic group U(9), which is cyclic of order 6 generated by 2, with units {1,2,4,5,7,8} = φ(9); 2 and 5 are its only generators. Standard elementary number theory, in Gauss and in every abstract-algebra text. The closure statements quantify that structure. Searched 2026-09-04, term "multiplicative group of units mod 9 cyclic order 6 generated by 2"; prior art found and credited. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.
